scope: Two concrete, low-attention crab locations only: Sand Crabs on the southern Hosidius coast and Ammonite Crabs in the Fossil Island Mushroom Forest. The word safe is a bounded planning label, not a claim that either location is risk-free, unattended-safe, suitable for every account, or a progression recommendation.

included: Current access, combat, tolerance, idle-combat, death-recovery, and location mechanics for the two named crab methods.
An observation-first readiness boundary covering aggression, current HP, selected gear, food, Prayer if used, emergency teleport or exit capability, and death/recovery state.
A proposed action that records an explicitly selected method/location and player-reported outcomes without simulating combat.
excluded: Strategy scoring, preferred ordering, guaranteed hourly rates, and guaranteed RNG outcomes.
Account readiness inference, unattended safety, a guaranteed session length, XP per hour, drops per hour, food use, survival chance, or an automatic reset/re-entry result.
A recommended location, gear setup, combat style, Prayer choice, food quantity, emergency teleport, travel route, training target, route order, or level 99 target.
Any generated combat XP, kill count, item drop, death, recovery cost, transport arrival, or RNG outcome.

source_catalog.use: Current Sand Crab locations, combat profile, dormant/active behaviour, tolerance reset, and variable drop boundary.
Current Ammonite Crab locations, combat profile, tolerance reset, low-level-food note, and variable drop boundary.
Current ten-minute standard-monster tolerance mechanic and the crab re-entry boundary.
Current combat idle, auto-retaliate, active-combat logout, and six-hour disconnect mechanics.
Current Fossil Island members access, Bone Voyage gate, and documented transport context.
Current Death's Office recovery boundary and ironman recovery-fee context.
Official historical provenance that Sand Crabs were added for the south Hosidius coast. Current runtime mechanics are taken from the current Wiki sources.

membership.claim: Both named NPC pages mark these crabs as members content.

sand-crab-hosidius-south-coast.claim: Sand Crabs are listed along the southern Hosidius coast; the official poll describes their addition to the coast south of Hosidius. This package records arrival as an observation and does not derive a travel route or arrival from membership.

ammonite-crab-mushroom-forest.claim: Ammonite Crabs are listed in the Mushroom Forest on Fossil Island. Reaching Fossil Island requires completion of Bone Voyage.

selection-boundary.claim: One concrete method/location must be selected: sand-crab-hosidius-south-coast or ammonite-crab-mushroom-forest. No selection is inferred from access, skill levels, inventory, or a prior observation.

tools.requirement: Player reports currently equipped combat gear and its condition before a session. This package does not prescribe gear or infer defensive adequacy.
Player reports one presently usable emergency teleport or another chosen exit plan, including relevant runes, charges, or item state if applicable. Availability and use are never inferred.

locations.claim: Sand Crabs occur on the southern Hosidius coast. Their current page lists combat level 15, 60 Hitpoints, a maximum hit of 1, crush attacks, and 30-second respawn time; dormant crabs activate when a player walks nearby.
Ammonite Crabs occur in the Fossil Island Mushroom Forest. Their current page lists combat level 25 and describes 100 Hitpoints with level 1 in the other combat stats.

transport_options.claim: The Fossil Island source documents the Digsite barge and a digsite-pendant route. They are access context only: neither is selected or treated as available to the player by this package.

inventory_inputs.requirement: Player-reported current and maximum HP before entry and at each attention check; no survivability threshold is supplied.
Player-reported food item, quantity, and remaining amount if food is carried. No food is mandatory in this package and no amount is assumed sufficient.
Player-reported immediately usable teleport or exit plan, with any required item/rune/charge state. The package neither chooses nor validates it as safe.

bank_inputs.requirement: Player-reported recovery funds/items and access plan, if any. Death's Office can recover eligible uncollected grave items; the player must separately observe the actual recovery state and any fee.

reusable_items.requirement: Selected equipped gear is observation-only. Ownership, charges, protection, and readiness are never inferred.

consumed_inputs.requirement: Food and any Prayer-restoration or other consumables are optional player-selected inputs. Record only reported consumption and remaining supplies; do not estimate use.

capacity_constraints.requirement: Available inventory slots and any space used by food, teleport/exit items, or drops are player-observed. This package does not auto-loot or calculate capacity.

interaction_cadence.claim: For standard monster tolerance, crabs become tolerant after ten minutes in the region; because active crabs are needed to fight them, re-entry beyond the tolerance region is required to restore crab aggression. This is a sourced mechanical reset, not an unattended-safety interval.

interval_seconds.meaning: aggression/tolerance boundary only; no XP, safety, or duration guarantee

interaction_cadence.claim: Combat auto-retaliation stops after more than twenty minutes without qualifying client interaction, even with Auto Retaliate enabled. This is an attention requirement, not a prompt to leave the account unattended.

interval_seconds.meaning: auto-retaliate idle boundary only; client input, health, aggression, and location must still be observed

interaction_cadence.claim: Before starting, after any return, and whenever the player chooses to check, record current aggression/targeting, HP, gear, food, Prayer if used, emergency exit capability, nearby hazards/players, and death/recovery state. Exact cadence is a player observation, not a sourced guarantee.

session_mechanics.entry_condition: Player confirms membership, explicitly selects one listed method/location, reports arrival and current readiness observations (aggression, HP, gear, food, Prayer if any, emergency exit, and death/recovery), and confirms combat start. This does not prove safety, survival, or output.

tolerance.claim: Standard tolerance is ten minutes before these crabs become tolerant; leaving and re-entering the tolerance region resets aggression.

combat-idle.claim: Auto-retaliation stops after more than twenty minutes of combat idle. A six-hour continuous-login disconnect can also end play, with warnings described by the idle source.

duration_evidence.boundary: No session duration, survival time, reset success, combat XP, or hourly result is guaranteed or calculated.

session_end_events: Observed crab tolerance/aggression expiry or inability to continue engaging at the selected location. [wiki-sand-crab-current, wiki-ammonite-crab-current, wiki-tolerance-current]
Observed combat auto-retaliate stop after the idle-combat boundary. [wiki-idle-current]

Observed low HP, food depletion, Prayer change, gear/teleport issue, unexpected damage/hazard, player choice to exit, logout/disconnect, or death; these are report-only stops and no outcome is inferred.

variable.description: Combat and Hitpoints XP are distinct from item drops. Record only the player-observed XP delta, selected style, and observed combat result; the package does not simulate hits, kills, XP, or an hourly rate.

Item drops are RNG outputs, not combat XP and not guaranteed. The Sand Crab and Ammonite Crab pages document drop tables; record only player-observed items and quantities, without calculating expected value or loot rate.

player_observed.description: Record only reported method/location, aggression/targeting state, current HP, gear, food, Prayer if used, emergency exit state, death/recovery state, XP delta, drops, consumables, logout/disconnect, and stop/re-entry result.

damage_sources: Sand Crabs use crush attacks and can damage the player; the player must observe actual targets and HP. [wiki-sand-crab-current]
Ammonite Crab combat and any location-specific or external threat must be observed at the time of play; this package does not model damage or assert a zero-damage setup. [wiki-ammonite-crab-current]
logout_behavior: While an active combat timer is running, manual logout is unavailable; the idle source describes the timer as ten seconds and reset by further hits. [wiki-idle-current]

The idle source describes a six-hour continuous-login disconnect and the combat-disconnect handling; treat any logout or disconnect as an observed session end, not a recovery guarantee. [wiki-idle-current]

Death's Office can hold eligible uncollected grave items, with recovery fees and ironman discount details described by its current page. Actual grave, office, fee, item, and recovery outcome remain player-observed. [wiki-deaths-office-current]
safety_and_logout.safe_boundary: Neither candidate is declared safe or unattended-safe. Start or continue only after the player has explicitly reported the selected location and current aggression, HP, gear, food, Prayer if any, emergency exit capability, and death/recovery situation; stop when any of those observations is no longer acceptable to that player.

mechanical_stop_conditions: Crab tolerance makes the crabs non-aggressive after ten minutes in the relevant tolerance region; active crabs are required to fight them. [wiki-sand-crab-current, wiki-ammonite-crab-current, wiki-tolerance-current]
Combat auto-retaliation stops after more than twenty minutes of client inactivity. [wiki-idle-current]
Player-observed stop: unsafe or changed aggression/targeting, HP, food, Prayer, gear, emergency exit, surrounding hazard, connection, death, or recovery state. No threshold is inferred.
mechanical_reentry_conditions: For either crab method, the player must leave and re-enter the tolerance region to reset aggression; the actual movement and restored targeting are player-observed. [wiki-tolerance-current, wiki-sand-crab-current, wiki-ammonite-crab-current]
A new session also requires an explicit method/location selection and fresh readiness observation; no prior session establishes continuing readiness.
reset_or_cleanup_requirements: Record remaining food/consumables, HP, Prayer if used, gear state, emergency exit state, observed XP/drops, and any death/recovery result. Do not convert unreported outcomes into state.

If a death occurred, recovery follows the observed grave/Death's Office state; the current Death's Office page describes its recovery mechanism but does not establish that the player can recover every item. [wiki-deaths-office-current]

facts.claim: One bounded production action requires available and acceptable selected-method observations plus a non-null combat readiness observation; it does not convert tolerance, access, or combat mechanics into survival or output claims.

actions.requirements: Available and acceptable selected Sand Crab or Ammonite Crab method/location observation plus a non-null combat readiness observation. Predicate semantics do not independently prove location access, so the action makes no access, arrival, aggression, survival, food, Prayer, death, or recovery claim.
actions.transition: Report-only variable output. Never simulate combat, assume survival, assert unattended safety, select a route, generate XP/drops, or create a recovery result.

edges.meaning: A non-null combat readiness observation is required before the bounded report-only activity becomes eligible; it makes no safety inference.

observations.boundary: All fields are player-reported at the time of use. Missing or stale fields block a start record rather than being inferred.
Combat XP, RNG drops, and all other results remain separate reported fields; an absent field is unknown, not zero.

conflicts_and_unknowns.detail: The current Sand Crab page's infobox labels Aggressive as No while its body states that dormant crabs attack after a player walks nearby and become tolerant after ten minutes. This package does not normalize a static aggression boolean; it requires player-observed aggression/targeting at the chosen spot.

No source proves that either method is safe for a particular account. Combat level, Hitpoints, gear, active targets, food, Prayer, emergency exit, player attention, connection, nearby conditions, and recovery state must be observed; this package deliberately supplies no threshold or recommendation.

The sources establish creature/drop mechanics but do not justify generating a player's combat XP, kill count, drops, food use, session length, or hourly result. All such outcomes remain player-observed, with drops marked RNG.

The included Jagex source is historical provenance for the Hosidius Sand Crab addition. Current runtime combat, tolerance, access, idle, and recovery mechanics are cited to current OSRS Wiki pages; no unsupported official-current claim is added.
